title: {{NAME}} and the League of Tiny Champions
moral: Every kind of strength matters, and the smallest hero can carry the most important power.

pages.content:
The city of Luminos rose around {{NAME}} like a skyline carved from candlelight and cloud. Towers of amber and rose crystal spiralled into a sky busy with wings, because in Luminos, the superheroes were fairies. Every last one of them.

{{NAME}} had arrived by accident, slipping through a revolving door in the local library that had seemed completely ordinary until it wasn't. Now he stood in a cobblestoned plaza the size of a football pitch, staring upward at a thousand different winged figures launching from rooftops, each one trailing a different colour of light behind them like living fireworks.

A signboard overhead read: THE FAIRY LEAGUE OF LUMINOS, KEEPING THE WONDER SAFE SINCE FOREVER. Below it, a much smaller sign read: JUNIOR HERO TRIALS TODAY, and below that, in very small writing: All sizes welcome.

{{NAME}} looked down at his cape, which his younger sister had painted the lightning bolt on last weekend. He squared his shoulders and walked toward the entrance.

pages.content:
The trial examiner was a fairy named Blaze, who was exactly as impressive as his name suggested. He was no bigger than a coffee mug, but his wings crackled with actual orange electricity, and he had the very particular stillness of someone who had once stopped a runaway comet with his bare hands.

He peered at {{NAME}} with one golden eye. "Strength trials are at Gate One," he said. "Speed at Gate Two. Power-beam testing at Gate Three." He paused, looking at the hand-painted lightning bolt on {{NAME}}'s cape with an expression {{NAME}} couldn't quite decode. "What's your power?"

{{NAME}} opened his mouth. He closed it again. The honest answer was that he wasn't entirely sure he had one, in the official superhero sense. What he had was this: he was very good at noticing things other people missed.

"Observation," he said carefully.

Blaze tilted his head. His crackling wings went still for just a moment. "We haven't had one of those in three hundred years," he said, and his golden eye was suddenly very bright.

pages.content:
The emergency siren sounded before the trials even began. A deep, resonant tone that sent every fairy in the plaza streaking skyward in a blur of wings and light.

Blaze grabbed {{NAME}}'s sleeve. "The Shadow Fog is back. It steals colour from everything it touches, and it's heading for the Crystal Heart, the power source of all of Luminos." His electric wings snapped urgently. "Every hero we send in loses sight of everything within seconds. The Fog absorbs light."

"But not observation," {{NAME}} said, and he was already moving.

They ran. Through twisting crystal streets, dodging the grey tendrils of the Shadow Fog that curled around corners like slow, curious fingers. Three fairy heroes, Spark, Mira, and a tiny armoured one called Bolt, joined them, their faces taut with frustration at a foe their powers couldn't touch.

The Crystal Heart pulsed at the centre of the tallest tower, visible through a fog-filled corridor. {{NAME}} moved slowly, studying every tendril, every drift and curl. There was a pattern. The Fog always moved away from a faint blue glow near the floor.

"Follow the blue light!" he called. "The Fog can't touch it!"

pages.content:
The Crystal Heart was enormous, a spinning gem the size of a beach ball, rotating slowly at the heart of the tower. The Shadow Fog pressed against its walls in a churning dark mass, drawn to it, feeding on its glow.

{{NAME}} watched. Breathed. Observed.

The Fog pulsed. It had a rhythm, expand and contract, like something breathing. And in the half-second between each pulse, it thinned. Just enough.

"Bolt," he said, turning to the armoured fairy. "You have the brightest armour. When I say NOW, fly straight through. Spark and Mira, follow on the left and right. You'll have two seconds before it closes."

Bolt's visor flashed. "You're certain?"

{{NAME}} had never been so certain of anything in his life. He watched the pulse. Counted its rhythm. Waited for the exact thinning moment.

"NOW."

Three fairy superheroes shot through the gap like comets. Three bursts of light, and then a sound like the whole crystal city ringing at once. The Shadow Fog recoiled, contracted, and vanished. The Crystal Heart blazed gold.

pages.content:
Luminos blazed back to life, colour flooding every crystal street in waves of amber and rose and gold. The fairy heroes landed around {{NAME}} in a wide circle, and the sound of a hundred tiny pairs of wings applauding was something like the patter of warm rain.

Blaze pinned a small badge to {{NAME}}'s cape, right next to the hand-painted lightning bolt. It was a golden eye, the emblem of the Observers, a branch of the League that had not had a new member for three hundred years.

The revolving door was waiting in the plaza when it was time to go. {{NAME}} stepped through, and the ordinary library was warm and quiet around him, the hum of the city outside faint and familiar.

He curled up that night with the golden eye badge on his bedside table, where he could see it catching the lamplight. His eyes grew heavy. And just before sleep took him completely, he found himself wondering: if the Shadow Fog had a rhythm, did it also have a source? And if it had a source, did it have a reason?
